page.overview:
Who is Jecht?

Jecht ['dʒɛktʰ] is a non-player character and a reluctant antagonist in Final Fantasy X. He is Tidus' father, was one of High Summoner Braska's legendary guardians, and a major blitzball star in his hometown. Jecht is a tall, muscular man with a tendency to drink heavily. He wields a large black sword in battle.

Jecht is a dark-skinned muscular man with long, unruly black hair and red eyes. He wears a pair of black shorts with an orange and red sash covering his right leg, a red headband, and a metal gauntlet and pauldron covering his left arm. He is barefoot and does not wear a shirt. His outfit appears to be a Zanarkand Abes jumper, similar to Tidus' uniform, with the straps undone. He has a black tattoo of the Zanarkand Abes' symbol on his chest. In his concept art and in Dissidia Final Fantasy, Jecht wields a black sword with red markings that resemble dolphins. He never wields the sword himself in Final Fantasy X. Braska's Final Aeon, on the other hand, wields a larger version of it and Jecht is mentioned to have fought with a sword during Braska's pilgrimage. The design of Jecht's greatsword, (called the Iconic Sword in Dissidia NT), resembles a ceremonial African Konda sword.

As Braska's Final Aeon, Jecht is a large, deformed version of his former self with brown scales and horns with crests of spikes emerging from his back and shoulders. He wears a larger version of his headband, his hair is white and emerges in tufts from the spikes around his head, and his eyes glow. His Zanarkand Abes tattoo is white and his body below the waist has another large crest of spikes partially covering his legs. His right hand is of normal proportions to his body and is used to wield his sword, while his left hand is a large claw.

Jecht is a surly bully who frequently refers to himself as "The Great Jecht" (Jecht-sama in the Japanese releases), arrogantly bestowing a respectful honorific onto himself, though he is genuinely titled "Sir Jecht" in Spira due being a guardian in a successful pilgrimage. Jecht considers himself the best blitzball player there is and loves fame, asking Braska several times if there will be celebratory events during, and especially after, their pilgrimage. Jecht's career hit a slump when he began drinking and it was rumored he was going to retire, though he was quick to deny this and claimed he could quit drinking if he chose. Jecht used to be emotionally abusive to Tidus, calling him "crybaby" and otherwise brushing him off or berating him.
